name: integration-tests
$tagsComment: `scope:shared` was here alongside `type:integration-test`. Nx permits a dependency when ANY tag matches, so `scope:shared` let any feature library import a harness that issues `DELETE /nuxeo/api/v1/path/...` and `Document.Trash`, while `type:integration-test` appeared in no rule in `eslint.config.mjs` and governed nothing. The single tag is now the only one, and `eslint.config.mjs` names it as a source but never as a permitted target — so this library may read the platform it drives and nothing may depend on it. Verified by importing it from a feature library and watching lint reject the edge.
// targets: to see all targets run: nx show project integration-tests --web

test.$comment: The unit half only, and it cannot become anything else: `vitest.unit.config.mts` includes `*.unit.spec.ts` and the `integration` target's config includes `*.integration.spec.ts`, so no file can match both. What runs here is the preflight's decision logic and the CLI's exit-code mapping with `fetch` stubbed — no Nuxeo, no Angular, nothing that a CI runner lacks.
test.$whyComment: The `integration` target does not run on CI, so until this existed the gate that decides whether the whole suite may run was itself unexercised there, and its exit-2-versus-exit-1 behaviour rested on one manual observation. A one-character edit could have collapsed the two codes with nothing going red.

integration.$comment: Named `integration`, not `test`, so no `-t test` invocation can reach the specs it runs. Those require a live Nuxeo; CI runners have none, so `nx affected -t test` and `nx run-many -t test` would fail every one of them on a precondition. An exclusion list in each workflow would work only for as long as everyone remembers to extend it — the name cannot be forgotten. The `test` target added beside this one does not weaken that: the two configs select on disjoint filename patterns, so a live spec has to be renamed before `-t test` can see it, and a rename is visible in a diff.
integration.$preflightComment: Preflight first, so an absent or empty Nuxeo reports as a precondition rather than as sixty-five product failures. Same shape as nuxeo-ui-e2e's `e2e`. Note that `nx` normalises a failed command to exit 1, so the preflight's exit 2 does NOT survive `nx run integration-tests:integration` — `npm run beta:integration` chains the same two commands with `&&` and does preserve it. That is why both exist, exactly as `beta:e2e` exists beside `nuxeo-ui-e2e:e2e`.
integration.$cacheComment: Deliberately NOT cached: the result depends on a live Nuxeo's contents, and a cached green would assert something about a server state that has since changed.

typecheck.$comment: `preflight-cli.ts` is neither a spec nor part of any bundle, so `spec-typecheck.mjs` does not reach it and there is no `build` target that would. Without this target the one file in the repository whose job is to exit with the right code would be the one file nothing type-checks.

$testTargetHistory: This project deliberately had NO `test` target, so that the live specs could not be reached by `-t test`. That reasoning survives — see the two targets above — but the blanket version of it had a cost that was not noticed until SonarCloud reported 0% coverage on the new code: `scripts/beta-harness/coverage-gate.mjs` discovers projects by the presence of `targets.test`, so the library was outside the ratchet entirely, and the preflight and its CLI were measured by nothing. The narrow `test` target puts only the server-free half in that population. `integration-harness.ts` and `user-fixtures.ts` are deliberately NOT unit-tested — they issue real DELETEs against a real repository, and a mocked version of that would assert the mock — so they sit in the report at 0% and drag the project's figure to ~28%. That is the honest number and it is meant to be read as debt, not patched away: they need no allowlist entry, because v8 instruments them and they are inside the denominator rather than invisible outside it, which is the state the allowlist exists to record. `nuxeo-ui-e2e` remains in the original position, with no `test` target and no entry.
